messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: High error rate on runtime-prod. Multiple container crashloops detected (SIGSEGV) across gpu-pool. Paging eng-oncall and runtime. Incident runbook: https://redwood/infra/incidents#runtime-segfaults :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-8721 triggered (sev=high) — paging @eng-oncall, @runtime, @sre. Escalation policy applied.

mike (eng-oncall): ack. I'm on it. Can folks paste recent pod logs & node names? I'm seeing 502s on internal health check dashboards.

sara (runtime): looking. Crashloop backtrace points at fused_kernels.cu -> compute_dispatch() SIGSEGV. Logs show repeated segfault immediately after model init. Suspect a kernel/library mismatch after last runtime-image rollout.

alice (sre): customer-visible: two customers (acme-corp, travelly-prod) seeing ~30% request failures to text-gen endpoints since 02:14 UTC. Routing fallback isn't fully engaged. We'll need to route traffic to fallback model or scale Dedicated capacity.

ram (ml-infra): listing affected pods: gpu-runtime-5f7d8 (node=gke-gpu-22), gpu-runtime-6a3b2 (node=gke-gpu-22), gpu-runtime-9c1d3 (node=gke-gpu-18). Node 22 shows multiple OOM and kernel messages earlier.

mike (eng-oncall): action plan: 1) cordon node gke-gpu-22 to prevent new pods landing 2) drain non-critical pods 3) rollback runtime image to previous tag on canary 4) enable model routing to cpu-fallback for affected customers. Anyone object? :thumbsup:

kate (product): please minimize customer impact; prefer routing to CPU fallback rather than full rollback if latency/customer SLO acceptable. We should notify account teams.

ram (ml-infra): quick logs snippet from gpu-runtime-5f7d8:

```
[2026-03-15T02:12:34Z] runtime: loading model config: bert-xxl-v2
[2026-03-15T02:12:35Z] gpu0: initializing fused-kernel v2.4.1
[2026-03-15T02:12:36Z] runtime: allocate kv-cache size=24MB
[2026-03-15T02:12:36Z] *** SIGSEGV @ 0x7f8c2b9e6a10 (fused_kernels.cu:214) ***
stack: libcudnn.so.8+0x1a3b2
stack: libcublas.so.11+0x4d21f
stack: runtime_engine.so+0x9f12
```

ram (ml-infra): also saw driver warnings on node 22: "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" in dmesg earlier. Might be underlying hardware flakiness layered with new fused kernel.

alice (sre): I'm cordoning gke-gpu-22 now. `kubectl cordon gke-gpu-22` -> done. Not draining until we confirm safe evictions.

sara (runtime): quick hypothesis: the new fused-kernel build (v2.4.1) depends on a different CUDA/cuDNN combination than what is on node 22 (driver 525.x vs required 530.x). That mismatch can cause mysterious segfaults. We should check `nvidia-smi` and `ldd` on runtime_engine.so.

mike (eng-oncall): good catch. ram can you run `kubectl exec` into one of the crashlooping pods (if it stays up long enough) and paste `nvidia-smi` + `ldd /opt/runtime/runtime_engine.so`? If not possible, copy logs from node.

ram (ml-infra): tried. Pod dies in ~1s but got `nvidia-smi` from node:
```
Wed Mar 15 02:11:58 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12 Driver Version: 525.85.12 CUDA Version: 11.8 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
and runtime_engine.so ldd shows dependencies on libcudnn.so.8 (expected) but the fused-kernel binary was built against cudnn 8.4 which expects driver >= 530.

alice (sre): if driver mismatch is the root cause we have two mitigation options: rollback runtime image to fused-kernel v2.3.x or reprovision node(s) with updated GPU driver. Rolling back is faster.

mike (eng-oncall): let's roll the canary back to v2.3.8 on runtime-canary by patching the deployment. ram will start the rollback, sara please prepare a configuration to force fallback to CPU for the two impacted customer routes.

sara (runtime): on it. Creating a quick route override in routing service to send acme-corp and travelly-prod to cpu-fallback-prod. Patch command:

```
POST /routing/overrides HTTP/1.1
Host: routing.redwood.internal
Content-Type: application/json

{"customers": ["acme-corp","travelly-prod"], "target": "cpu-fallback-v1", "ttl": 3600}
```

ram (ml-infra): rolling back canary now: `kubectl set image deployment/runtime-canary runtime=redwood/runtime:2.3.8` -> update started.

infra-bot: Autoscaler detected surge in pod restarts; paused autoscaling temporarily to prevent noisy scaling and spreading.

mike (eng-oncall): watching canary logs. If stable for 3 mins we'll promote rollback to primary. Also setting temporary circuit-breaker: reject large-batch requests to reduce memory pressure.

~3 minutes later~

ram (ml-infra): runtime-canary at 2.3.8 is stable. No segfault observed for ~5 min. Promoting rollback to runtime-prod now with rolling restart of 5 pods at a time.

sara (runtime): routing override applied; acme and travelly now hitting cpu-fallback. Latency higher but error rate down to <1%. Product notified.

mike (eng-oncall): partial mitigation success. However node gke-gpu-22 still has hardware errors in dmesg: `NVRM: GPU fell off bus` and other ECC warnings. Marking node for reprovisioning. `gcloud compute instances delete` after draining.

alice (sre): customers restored to functional state. Raising incident severity to "mitigated" and starting post-incident tasks: inventory driver versions across all gpu nodes, add pre-deploy compatibility check for fused-kernel builds, add automatic route fallback when crashloop rate > X.

sara (runtime): follow-ups I'm adding to the ticket: (1) add an integration test that runs fused kernel init on a matrix of driver versions in CI, (2) add feature-flag to disable fused kernel on a per-cluster basis, (3) capture core dumps on segfaulting pods for offline analysis (commands below).

```
# enable core dumps on node
sudo sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/tmp/cores/core-%e-%p-%t
sudo sysctl -w fs.suid_dumpable=2
# in container images set ulimit
ulimit -c unlimited
# collect backtrace
gdb -batch -ex "thread apply all bt full" -ex quit /opt/runtime/runtime_engine.so corefile > /tmp/coredump_bt.txt
```

ram (ml-infra): I saved core+logs to s3://redwood-incidents/PD-8721/ and updated the incident ticket. Node gke-gpu-22 set for reprovisioning; new nodes will have driver 530+ installed.

mike (eng-oncall): final status: runtime image rollback to 2.3.8 completed across prod, routing override in place for impacted customers, gke-gpu-22 cordoned + reprovision planned, autoscaler unpaused with limits. Impact: degraded latency for two customers during mitigation window but functional.

kate (product): notified account teams and customers via status page. Thanks team for fast mitigation.

alice (sre): I'm closing the immediate paging. We'll run a postmortem doc and link action items. Next steps: schedule driver upgrades across pool, add CI compatibility matrix, implement per-cluster feature-flag and canary check.

mike (eng-oncall): thanks all. I'll hand off to oncall-next for the rest of the night. Oncall-next: please monitor restart rates and routing overrides.

oncall-handoff: mike -> sarah-next (oncall-next). handoff-ts: 1905001987

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: PD-8721 marked mitigated at 02:35 UTC. Postmortem assigned to sara (runtime) and ram (ml-infra).
